claim: On 11 September 2026 traffickers took five teenagers and young men (two aged 16, two 18 and one 20) from Mithachhari, Ramu, by CNG auto-rickshaw on the pretext of visiting Teknaf's Marine Drive, blindfolded and held them, beat them and collected ransom from their families in instalments while planning to send them by sea to Indonesia and Malaysia; SRB-15 (Special Response Battalion 15) rescued them on 20 September at Khonkarpara ghat near Sabrang Zero Point, Teknaf, and arrested Md Anas alias Munna (21).
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Malaysia: boats and land crossings
why_new: New 2026 case; adds a tourist-trip lure aimed at Bangladeshi teenagers, not Rohingya.

claim: A boat of irregular migrants from Myanmar's Rakhine state capsized off the Baharchhara coast of Teknaf at dawn on 22 September 2026, killing a Rohingya woman, Chhura Khatun (28), and her 9-year-old son; of the 16 rescued, eight were Bangladeshis who told police they had been taken to Myanmar about a year earlier on the promise of Malaysia, kept in various parts of Myanmar for a year, and put on the boat for Malaysia the night before.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Malaysia: boats and land crossings
why_new: New 2026 case of Bangladeshis held a year in Myanmar on a Malaysia promise; fits the guide's 'journeys sold as going through Malaysia end in Myanmar'.

claim: On the night of 1 October 2026 the navy ship BNS Khalid Bin Walid, alerted by fishermen, rescued 76 people from a wooden boat whose engine had failed and which was sinking about 81 km west of the St Martin's Island lighthouse; the navy said 65 men, women and children aboard, some lured with good jobs and some kidnapped and held in remote parts of Teknaf, were being trafficked to Malaysia by way of the Myanmar and Thai coasts, and it detained 11 alleged traffickers.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Malaysia: boats and land crossings
why_new: New 2026 case.

claim: On 5 November 2026 a joint army, BGB and police operation freed 57 people from a traffickers' den in the deep hills of Rangikhali, Teknaf, where they were being tortured for ransom and were to be put on a trawler to Malaysia that night; a soldier, Md Titas Sheikh (27), was shot dead in a gunfight, five ring members were detained, and police said one of the 57 was identified as a trafficker.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Malaysia: boats and land crossings
why_new: New November 2026 case.

claim: Nur Kamal (21) of Daganbhuiyan, Feni, told Prothom Alo in November 2026 that someone added him to a WhatsApp group offering to take him to Malaysia free of cost, with payment due only after arrival; he left home on 2 November and on reaching Cox's Bazar was taken to a hut in the Teknaf hills, held under 10 to 12 armed guards and beaten.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Malaysia: boats and land crossings
placement: How it is sold / Other lures
why_new: New lure: 'free now, pay on arrival' through WhatsApp groups, in the month the government was advertising zero-cost Malaysia jobs.

claim: Victims freed on 5 November 2026 said people were handed to the traffickers for money: S M Asaduzzaman (50) of Saltha, Faridpur, said a man he met in Kutupalong camp lured him with work and handed him over for Tk 10,000, then he agreed a Tk 2 lakh release deal; Md Saiful Islam of Ukhiya said a broker named Nur Ali handed him over and the traffickers said they had bought him and another man for Tk 1 lakh, and that captives who tried to flee were beaten and chained.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Malaysia: boats and land crossings
why_new: Adds the price at which people are sold into the dens (Tk 10,000 a head; Tk 1 lakh for two), which the cross-country doc lacks.

claim: On the evening of 7 November 2026 BGB rescued nine people, including two aged 16 and 17, gathered at South Lombori ghat, Teknaf Sadar union, to be taken to Malaysia by sea, while 10 to 15 ring members fled by boat; the rescued said men were lured with good jobs and women with marriage to suitable grooms in Malaysia, the Teknaf BGB battalion commander said.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Malaysia: boats and land crossings
why_new: New November 2026 case.

claim: On the evening of 16 November 2026, 72 people, mostly Rohingya and the rest from Teknaf, Naikhongchhari and other districts, who had paid brokers Tk 10,000 to 15,000 each, were taken by small fishing boats from Mithapanir Chhara ghat, Teknaf, to a large wooden trawler; after rough seas from a cyclone kept it near St Martin's Island and the crew and brokers quarrelled, the crew landed them at Laboni Point on Cox's Bazar beach late on 20 November and fled, and police rescued 28 while the rest ran away.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Malaysia: boats and land crossings
why_new: New November 2026 case, with the 2026 boarding price (Tk 10,000 to 15,000).

claim: Kuddus Bepari (33) of Majumdarkandi, Rajoir, Madaripur, who had worked in Malaysia for 7 years and came home in August 2024 to see his newborn child, was frustrated because the Malaysian labour market was not going well, and the local broker Monir Sheikh, learning of it, lured him into a Tk 16 lakh 'body contract' to reach Italy through Libya, according to police, family and local sources.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Recruited while abroad or just back
why_new: The cross-country 'In Malaysia' bullet has only a general BRAC statement; this is a named case of a Malaysia worker on home leave recruited onto the Libya route.

claim: The CID arrested a woman (named Fabiha Jerin and also Tamanna in its statements), a partner in Dream Home Travels and Tours Ltd, at Dhaka airport on 5 February 2025 as she was about to flee to Nepal, in a case filed at Banani police station by the wife of a wounded victim; the CID said she confessed and that her brother Tuhin, in Russia, had encouraged people to go to the war.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Russia: recruited into the war
why_new: Named travel agency and arrest not in the cross-country guide.

claim: CID (the police Criminal Investigation Department) said in June 2025 that a ring lured 10 people with jobs as cleaners or cooks in a chocolate factory in Russia at Tk 2-2.5 lakh a month, sent them first to Saudi Arabia on Umrah visas, had them perform Umrah, then took them to Russia and sold them to a man called Sultan, who handed them to the Russian army.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Russia: recruited into the war
why_new: The cross-country Russia section has RMMRU's general statement that many go via Saudi Arabia on tourist or Umrah visas [RU0030]; this adds a documented CID case with the job lure and pay promised.

claim: CID arrested Fabiha Jerin alias Tamanna, a partner of Dream Home Travels and Tours Limited of Banani, Dhaka, at Dhaka airport on 5 February 2025 as she was fleeing to Nepal, and arrested the alleged ringleader Muhammad Alamgir Hossain (40) of Lohagara, Chattogram at Chattogram's Shah Amanat airport in June 2025; CID said Alamgir, who went to Russia on a student visa in 2008 and became a citizen by marriage, had taken 50 people to Russia on three visa categories.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Russia: recruited into the war
why_new: Names a travel agency and ringleader in the Russia route not in the cross-country section.

claim: To pay broker Monir Sheikh, Kuddus Bepari wrote two bighas of land worth Tk 40 lakh to the broker's wife, Hamida Begum; Monir ran a tailoring shop at Rajoir bazar until about two years earlier, married his three daughters to men living in Libya whom locals say are linked to traffickers and mafias there, has bought land worth at least Tk 5 crore in his wife's name in seven months, and, locals say, makes each contract for Tk 16 lakh.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: The contract price and the final price
why_new: Shows payment in land rather than cash and the broker-to-Libya family chain; not in cross-country.

claim: A broker of another Madaripur ring, speaking anonymously in February 2025, said local brokers only collect people and money for Bangladeshi brokers living in Libya, taking Tk 12 lakh to send a person to Libya and Tk 4 lakh more for the 'game' (the sea crossing), and that most local brokers in Madaripur now work for Miraj Howlader of Mridhakandi, Shikarmangal union, Kalkini, whom he called a big mafia figure in Libya.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: The contract price and the final price
why_new: Gives the split of the Tk 16 lakh price (12 + 4); not in cross-country.

claim: Under the new migrant-worker insurance contract made on 12 March 2023, as Prothom Alo reported in January 2024, a worker gets no insurance benefit for suicide or self-harm within six months of cover starting, death or illness from HIV/AIDS or similar disease, death in dangerous sports or adventure activities, death from alcohol or drug addiction, death in war, riot or an attack by criminals, or execution under a court sentence.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: What does the migrant insurance cover?
why_new: The cross-country insurance section lists what it pays but no exclusions; the Saudi guide says only that suicide claims are often rejected [E0097]. Relevant to Saudi executions (What can get you jailed or deported).

claim: Under the March 2023 insurance contract, a worker who dies naturally or in an accident during the cover period, or within 90 days after it ends, is paid the full Tk 10 lakh, and when a worker dies abroad the money goes to the worker's bank account after the body comes home without any application, according to the Welfare Board and Jiban Bima Corporation (January 2024).
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: What does the migrant insurance cover?
why_new: The 90-day grace after expiry is not in either guide; the Saudi guide says no application is needed if the body comes home [E0013] but not that the money goes to the worker's own bank account.

claim: By Jiban Bima Corporation's count, 32,24,343 workers went abroad from the start of the compulsory migrant insurance in late 2019 to the end of 2023, and only 1,397 workers or families claimed on it; in fiscal 2022-23 the Welfare Board paid Tk 31 crore 72 lakh 10 thousand in death insurance to the families of 860 workers.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: What does the migrant insurance cover?
why_new: Claim and payout figures are not in either guide.

claim: Prothom Alo reported in January 2024 that disability and early-return benefits must be claimed, that the government agencies hold no information on workers who come back disabled or within six months, and that people involved said there is no special effort to tell workers about the insurance before they leave.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: What does the migrant insurance cover?
why_new: Explains why the Tk 50,000 job-loss and disability benefits are rarely claimed; not in either guide.

claim: A 2023 study by RMMRU (the Refugee and Migratory Movements Research Unit) found that 31% of migrant women workers' deaths abroad were unnatural, from accidents and suicide.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: What does the migrant insurance cover?
why_new: Not in either guide; bears on how often the suicide exclusion bites for women.

claim: Probashi Kallyan Bank's managing director Md. Mujibur Rahman said in March 2024 that loan conditions for returnee women had been eased: a woman whose husband or family won't take her back can borrow without a fixed address, her loan carries no service charge, and loans up to Tk 1 lakh need no equity, though few women apply.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: What help is there when I come back?
placement: other: PKB loans for returnee women
why_new: The Saudi guide's PKB reintegration loan (Reintegration loan (PKB)) needs a Union Parishad address certificate and charges 0.5%+0.5% fees [E0115, E0116]; this eased rule for returnee women is not there.

claim: Hasan Imam of the Center for Development Communication said in December 2025 that the government's reintegration policy, begun in 2022, received final approval in 2025, with six objectives: employment and financial self-reliance, entrepreneurship, social reintegration and health care, psychosocial support, support for exploited and abused women, and sustainability.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: What help is there when I come back?
why_new: Cross-country mentions a reintegration policy without its approval date or objectives.

claim: According to Prothom Alo (February 2026), the Bangladesh government supplies antiretroviral (ARV) drugs free, but counselling, mental health support and livelihood rehabilitation for returnees are very limited; Mir of the youth organisation Brave Dimension Global said one deported worker got counselling not from any government agency but from a private organisation.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: What help is there when I come back?
why_new: Cross-country: help for returnees deported with HIV.

claim: According to the national AIDS/STD control programme of Bangladesh's Directorate General of Health Services, 1,891 people were found infected with HIV in Bangladesh from December 2024 to November 2025, 12% of them people who had come back from abroad.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: What help is there when I come back?
why_new: Statistic; keep only if the HIV item is added.

claim: The Prime Minister's spokesman said on 18 April 2026 that the government had begun work on a 'Probashi card' for migrants; no details were given.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: What help is there when I come back?
why_new: Announcement only; a reviewer could turn it into a Need to know.

claim: A study by OKUP (Ovibashi Karmi Unnayan Program) found 94% of women workers forced to return had suffered regular physical and mental abuse abroad and 47% sexual harassment, according to a Prothom Alo editorial (19 October 2026) citing Prothom Alo of 13 September 2026.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: What if I'm abused? Where can I go?
why_new: Not Saudi-specific; not in guide.

claim: Migration experts told Prothom Alo in February 2024 that migrants already abroad collect job demand from their employers and send it to acquaintances and relatives at home, and that about 90% of demand letters reach Bangladesh this way.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: What is a demand letter?
why_new: How demand letters reach Bangladesh; not specific to Malaysia, where demand goes through FWCMS.

claim: According to Prothom Alo (February 2026), an HIV-negative certificate is compulsory before going abroad, but pre-departure briefings say very little about HIV, safe behaviour or the right to health care abroad.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: What is the pre-departure orientation (PDO)?
why_new: Cross-country PDO content gap.

claim: Expatriates' Welfare Ministry officials said in October 2026 that BMET's pre-departure training is only a three-day workshop in which nothing is taught well, and that workers need training on the destination's type of work, conditions, working hours and staying healthy.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: What is the pre-departure orientation (PDO)?
why_new: Ministry officials' own view of the PDO; the cross-country doc has similar views from a federation and UNDP expert.

claim: The expatriates' welfare minister said on 26 October 2026 that work is under way on technology at BMET to check visa validity quickly, and that an open email service to settle any complaint is being launched and publicised.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Where to complain and get help
why_new: New: announced (not yet live) complaint email and visa-check tool; not Saudi-specific. Need to know: what is the address and is it live?

claim: When a mentally ill worker or one with no address is found at Dhaka's Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, the Probashi Kallyan (expatriate welfare) desk or the Airport Armed Police phone Al-Amin (Nayan), manager of BRAC's Migration Welfare Centre, who by the US State Department's account at its June 2024 TIP Hero award had helped at least 34,000 returnees and trafficking victims.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Where victims and families get help
why_new: Cross-country item 12 lists BRAC's airport help but not how the airport desk and Armed Police route vulnerable returnees to it.

claim: Al-Amin, who received the US State Department's TIP Hero award on 24 June 2024, said he was himself trafficked when he went to work in Malaysia; Prothom Alo reported that this was in 2007, that he came home the same year, that he started work in BRAC's migration programme in 2017, and that he is president of Anirban Survivor Voice, the largest network of trafficking survivors in Bangladesh.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Where victims and families get help
placement: other: who runs BRAC's airport help
why_new: Background on the person behind BRAC's Migration Welfare Centre and Anirban Survivor Voice, both named elsewhere in the cross-country guide.

claim: By BMET data reported on 18 December 2024, more than 11 lakh workers went abroad in 2022, 13 lakh in 2023 and 9 lakh in the first 11 months of 2024; overseas employment fell further after Malaysia closed in June 2024 and rose again on Saudi Arabia, which took 60% of the year's workers and more than 80% in October and November.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Which countries can I go to for work right now?
why_new: Corridor context (Malaysia's closure and Saudi dependence) for the cross-country doc; historical, may be superseded.

claim: By the Ami Probashi 2024 annual report, 10,09,146 Bangladeshi workers went abroad in 2024, 27% fewer than the 13,90,811 of 2023, with 62% going to Saudi Arabia; enrolment in technical training centre courses fell to 1,12,166 from 2,36,270, and women's share of BMET registrations rose from 2.78% to 4.79%.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Which countries can I go to for work right now?
why_new: Cross-country corridor numbers for 2024.

claim: According to BMET, Bangladeshi workers went to 141 of the 168 countries on its list in 2025, 90% of them to just five countries; 13 countries received one worker each.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Which countries can I go to for work right now?

claim: RMMRU said in March 2026 that 4,663 Bangladeshis went to Russia in 2025 against 993 the year before, and that a ring had begun recruiting migrants with promises of good pay and Russian citizenship, part of which, together with unscrupulous Russian rings, was sending Bangladeshi workers to the Russia-Ukraine war.
target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Which countries can I go to for work right now?

target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Which countries can I go to for work right now?

why_new: Official 2025 totals; CONFLICT with 11,16,399 cited from BMET in a 3 April 2026 column (article fa1e9f68).

target_section: CROSS-COUNTRY: Who can I call for help while abroad?
